LAB-SEC-101.title: Possible backdoor: runs code downloaded over HTTP
LAB-SEC-101.fix: Code from a web response should never reach load(); this is how known FiveM backdoors take over a server. Remove it unless you wrote it and trust the server it calls.

LAB-SEC-102.title: Runs code built from encoded or obfuscated text
LAB-SEC-102.fix: Find out what the decoded text does before starting the resource; ship readable source (or Cfx escrow) instead of hidden code.

LAB-SEC-103.title: Obfuscated data in the code
LAB-SEC-103.fix: Long escaped-byte, base64 or hex strings and long string.char lists hide what the code does. Check what they decode to.

LAB-SEC-104.title: Reads a server secret
LAB-SEC-104.fix: A resource has no reason to read the license key or RCON password; database credentials only belong in the database resource. Find out where the value goes.

LAB-SEC-105.title: HTTP request to a raw IP or a hidden address
LAB-SEC-105.fix: Legitimate integrations call named, documented hosts. Find out who runs the address and what is sent there.

LAB-SEC-106.title: Runs shell commands or writes outside its own resource
LAB-SEC-106.fix: os.execute and io.popen run programs on the host; writing other resources' files is how backdoors spread. Keep file writes inside GetResourcePath(GetCurrentResourceName()).

LAB-SEC-107.title: Code hidden behind a long run of spaces
LAB-SEC-107.fix: Legitimate code is never pushed out of view. This is how a known FiveM backdoor hides a loader that runs remote code on player clients: delete the hidden part and treat the package as compromised.

LAB-PKG-004.title: Executable or system script in the package
LAB-PKG-004.fix: FXServer never needs .exe, .dll, .bat, .cmd, .ps1, .sh, .vbs, .jar or .scr files to run a resource. A C# resource (one that contains a *.net.dll) may ship .dll assemblies; those are not flagged. Don't run the others; ask the author why they are included.

LAB-PKG-005.title: Archive entry with an unsafe path
LAB-PKG-005.fix: Entries with '..', absolute paths or drive letters can write outside the folder they are extracted to. They were skipped; extract the archive with a tool that refuses them.
